That's the last piece. Here's everything we've settled together, in plain terms — this is the scope I'd build.

**Saving & automatic details**
- Paste a link and save it in one step; it appears at the top of your list.
- The title, description, site icon, and a preview image (when the page has one) are filled in automatically. If a page's details can't be read, the link is still saved and you can type them in yourself.

**Organizing**
- Add tags and a note while saving (both optional), with suggestions from tags you already use and an easy way to create new ones.
- Edit a bookmark's title, description, tags, note, or even its link later — changing the link can optionally refresh the details.
- Notes are written in Markdown and shown nicely formatted.

**Keeping the list useful**
- Mark things "Read later" and see just those; archive links to keep them without cluttering the main list; restore or delete (with a brief undo) as needed.
- Three views — All, To read, Archived — each with a count.
- Sort by newest, oldest, title, or recently updated.

**Finding again**
- A powerful search across title, description, note, tags, and link — with exact phrases, tag-specific searches, and AND/OR/NOT with grouping — plus a tag filter bar. Save any search (query + filter + view) to reuse with one click.

**Working in bulk**
- Select several bookmarks, or everything in the current view, to tag, untag, mark read/unread, archive, or delete together.

**Keeping copies safe**
- Preserve a full-page copy of a bookmark (kept as a self-contained file; PDFs kept as PDFs), automatically or on demand, and optionally also save it to the Internet Archive.

**Moving in and out**
- Import your browser's bookmarks (folders become tags, duplicates skipped, original titles/dates/tags preserved) and export as a browser file or a full backup.

**Comfort**
- Display preferences: light/dark/match-system, density, text size, show/hide previews, how many per page (with paging), which view to open on, and default sort.

It's a personal, single-user web app, and we've walked through the empty, error, overflow, and duplicate situations for these along the way.

**May I start building this scope now?** Once you approve, I'll switch into development and implement exactly what we've confirmed here.
